title: Gravity and Orbit
premise: Tamsin Crane, an insurance investigator who catalogues impossible accidents, is the last living keeper of a deep-space beacon no one remembers commissioning. When the salvage ship Meridian returns from a decades-long voyage with its crew aged backward into children, two rival fleets converge on the beacon, each claiming it as proof of their own origin myth. Tamsin discovers the beacon was built by his own grandfather to broadcast a fabricated distress signal that keeps the fleets from open war — and that the lie is failing. To preserve the peace, he must choose between exposing the truth and becoming the beacon's next false voice, ending with him transmitting the lie himself as the child-crew of the Meridian watch him become what he spent his life investigating.
about_author: C. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years adjudicating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose lighthouse they once helped decommission.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Catastrophes
chapters.summary: Tamsin Crane files routine reports on impossible accidents — a cargo lift that fell upward, a hull breach with no hole — while quietly maintaining a beacon whose maintenance contracts trace back to a company that never existed. POV: Tamsin. The emotional beat is lonely competence: a man fluent in other people's disasters but unable to name why he keeps tending something nobody asked for.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: The salvage ship Meridian docks with a crew of adults aged backward into children who remember futures that haven't happened. Tamsin's investigation collides with two armed fleets converging on the beacon, each reading the anomaly as vindication. POV alternates between Tamsin and Ilsa Vey, the fleet commander's daughter aboard the Meridian. The beat is vertigo — certainty dissolving as Tamsin finds his own family name in the ship's oldest logs.

chapters.title: Inheritance of a Lie
chapters.summary: Tamsin decrypts the beacon's core and learns his grandfather built it to broadcast a forged distress call that froze both fleets in place for sixty years; the signal is decaying, and war will follow within days. Ilsa's faction wants the truth published; the fleets want the beacon seized. POV: Tamsin, with Ilsa pressing him to burn the archive. The beat is moral collapse into clarity — justice outside the law means choosing which lie deserves to survive.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: As both fleets power weapons, Tamsin climbs the beacon tower to hand-transmit the dying signal, knowing the lie will need a living voice forever after. Ilsa chooses to stand with him rather than expose him, inheriting the secret alongside the guilt. POV: shared final chapter, closing on the child-crew watching from below. The beat is solemn transformation: Tamsin becomes the accident he could never explain, and peace holds on a foundation of deliberate deceit.
